rows.label: High-fit unconstrained text model
rows.clinical_analogy: A fluent LLM summary fits notes but violates a known physiologic invariant.
rows.reason: High empirical fit is not enough when no auditable structural constraint is specified.

rows.label: Physics-informed model with large residual
rows.clinical_analogy: A physiology-aware predictor still leaves an unsafe conservation-law residual.
rows.reason: The structural residual remains too large for an assurance claim.

rows.label: PIKS-style linear constraint with universal kernel
rows.clinical_analogy: A method-level claim that linear constraints are being satisfied in a synthetic monitor.
rows.reason: The synthetic case supports a bounded structural-consistency claim.

rows.label: Misspecified rough target outside native RKHS
rows.clinical_analogy: A noisy or rough patient trajectory where universality does not remove rate uncertainty.
rows.reason: Universal kernels can support consistency while rough targets still require rate/stress audits.

rows.label: Boundary measurements with interior differential constraint
rows.clinical_analogy: Boundary observations plus interior mechanistic constraints in a synthetic physiology model.
rows.reason: Boundary observations and interior constraints are method evidence, not clinical validation.

rows.label: Nonlinear or unmodeled medical mechanism
rows.clinical_analogy: A nonlinear disease mechanism is being forced into a linear-constraint audit.
rows.reason: PIKS-style guarantees for linear constraints do not cover the stated mechanism.

capstone_interpretation: Physics-informed evidence can support structural consistency claims, especially for auditable linear constraints, but it does not by itself authorize patient-outcome or treatment claims.
